title: SU Draconis: an RR Lyrae star, TESS sector 15
credit: TESS, sector 15 (NASA; SPOC light curve from MAST)

license.statement: NASA mission data, released through MAST without restriction on reuse. MAST asks that work using its data acknowledge the mission and the archive.

columns.name: time
columns.description: bin centre: t0 + (index + 0.5) x binDays, in BTJD

columns.name: flux error
columns.description: propagated PDCSAP error over the median, one sigma, per bin

masks.rule: any nonzero flag drops the cadence
a cadence without a finite value in all three is dropped
a bin with fewer than 3 kept cadences is dropped

reductions: 10-minute bins average up to 5 two-minute cadences each; the pulsation's rise from minimum to maximum, 0.155 of a cycle or about two and a half hours, spans fifteen bins.
Flux is kept in steps of 20 ppm and its error in steps of 5 ppm (binned-relative-flux/2): the star swings from about 0.77 to 1.46 of its median, far past the 3.3% that binned-relative-flux/1 holds.

source.archive: MAST (Barbara A. Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes)

citations.text: TESS Light Curves - All Sectors, STScI/MAST
Monson et al. 2017, AJ 153, 96, Table 1 (period of SU Dra)

steps: Read tess2019226182529-s0015-0000000142848794-0151-s_lc.fits with the SDK's readFits(), pinned by its checksum.
Mask, normalize and bin it with the SDK's binTessLightCurve(), the pipeline every TESS pack uses: QUALITY 0 and finite values only, divided by the median, 10-minute bins of at least 3 cadences.
Encode it as binned-relative-flux/2, flux in steps of 20 ppm.

assumptions: PDCSAP flux has had instrumental systematics and crowding removed by SPOC; that correction is used as published. Its crowding estimate is sound here: CROWDSAP is 0.985.
Times are barycentric dynamical time for the target, as SPOC corrects them.
The star's period does not change measurably across one sector. RR Lyrae periods drift by parts in a billion a day.

validation.check: a 20-harmonic Fourier series fits best at the published period, within 0.00005 d
